# geoBoundaries CGAZ Global Administrative Boundaries

> A mirror of geoBoundaries' Comprehensive Global Administrative Zones (CGAZ)
> composite as cloud-native GeoParquet and PMTiles: 218 country polygons, 3,224
> first-level units, 49,349 second-level units, plus a 3.6 MB name search index
> across all three levels. Static files on object storage, no API, no
> credentials. Produced by geoBoundaries at William & Mary geoLab; this catalog
> republishes, it does not produce.

Public root: https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/geoboundaries-catalog/catalog.json

This is a Portolan catalog, which is STAC 1.1.0 plus the Portolan profile. Every
file is readable in place over HTTPS range requests. Four collections, each with
a `collection.json`, a `README.md` for humans, an `AGENTS.md` for machine
clients, a GeoParquet file, a PMTiles archive and three to four MapLibre styles.

License: CC-BY-4.0. Attribution is required, and the required citation is
Runfola et al. (2020), PLoS ONE 15(4): e0231866.

This is NOT a byte-for-byte mirror. It repairs 38 double-encoded names and
1,275 invalid geometries, assigns the CRS the upstream files omit, drops one
all-NULL column, and adds a name search index and simplified display geometry.
Every deviation, with how to reproduce it and how to get vanilla geoBoundaries,
is in changes-from-upstream.md.

## Read these first

- [Catalog agent guide](https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/geoboundaries-catalog/AGENTS.md): the collections, the join keys, and the four traps that produce wrong answers.
- [Catalog README](https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/geoboundaries-catalog/README.md): what is here, the license, the provenance, and the exact upstream release.
- [Root catalog.json](https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/geoboundaries-catalog/catalog.json): the STAC entry point.
- [Changes from vanilla geoBoundaries](https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/geoboundaries-catalog/changes-from-upstream.md): every repair and every addition, with how to reproduce each one.

## Collections

- [adm0 — Country Boundaries](https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/geoboundaries-catalog/adm0/collection.json): 218 rows, 97 MB GeoParquet, 55 row groups of 4 rows. [agent guide](https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/geoboundaries-catalog/adm0/AGENTS.md)
- [adm1 — First-Level Administrative Boundaries](https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/geoboundaries-catalog/adm1/collection.json): 3,224 rows, 76 MB, 51 row groups of 64 rows. [agent guide](https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/geoboundaries-catalog/adm1/AGENTS.md)
- [adm2 — Second-Level Administrative Boundaries](https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/geoboundaries-catalog/adm2/collection.json): 49,349 rows, 101 MB, 97 row groups of 512 rows. [agent guide](https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/geoboundaries-catalog/adm2/AGENTS.md)
- [names — Name Search Index](https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/geoboundaries-catalog/names/collection.json): 52,398 rows, 3.6 MB, sorted by folded name, 35 row groups of 1,536 rows. [agent guide](https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/geoboundaries-catalog/names/AGENTS.md)

## Start a query

```sql
INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial; INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;

SELECT name, country_name, level, name_dupes
FROM 'https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/geoboundaries-catalog/names/cgaz_names.parquet'
WHERE name_norm LIKE 'zurich%'
ORDER BY level;
```

## The four things that produce wrong answers

1. `shapeType` is not the level of the file. CGAZ fills gaps with the next
   coarser level, so the ADM2 file holds 312 first-level units and 2 whole
   countries, and all three files hold the same 20 disputed areas.
2. `shapeGroup` is not always an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code. The 20 disputed-area
   rows carry `111` through `129`, except Western Sahara which uses `ESH`.
3. The ADM0 file has no `shapeID` column. Join at level 0 on `shapeGroup`.
4. Nothing in CGAZ links a second-level unit to the first-level unit containing
   it. There is no parent key at any level.
5. The `*_display.parquet` files are buffered OUTWARD on purpose, so
   neighbouring units overlap. Draw and filter with them; measure and clip
   with the full-resolution files.

## Optional

- [Upstream geoBoundaries](https://www.geoboundaries.org/): the authoritative source, including the full-resolution per-country releases this catalog does not mirror.
- [CGAZ download page](https://www.geoboundaries.org/globalDownloads.html): the upstream description of what CGAZ is and how it differs from the per-country files.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/portolan-mirrors/geoboundaries-catalog): the pipeline that built this catalog, the per-collection `.portolan/metadata.yaml` provenance records, and the issue tracker.
- [Runfola et al. (2020)](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0231866): the paper geoBoundaries asks you to cite.
- [Portolan specification](https://github.com/portolan-sdi/portolan-spec): what this catalog conforms to.
- [cn-geocoder-overture](https://github.com/portolan-mirrors/cn-geocoder-overture): an experimental sibling catalog built from Overture Maps divisions, with city and locality coverage and multilingual names. Same column contract, ODbL rather than CC BY, so share-alike rather than attribution-only.
